title: The C input line that opens a security hole (use fgets)
description:
C never checks how much text you type into a buffer. Read a name with the old gets() function and a long enough input writes straight past the end of your array and corrupts memory — a classic real-world security bug. This Short shows the safe replacement from the C Mastery Path Arrays & Strings lesson: fgets with an explicit buffer size, plus the trailing-newline quirk you have to strip.

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/c-mastery-path/level-1/05-arrays-strings/

#Shorts

beats.narration: C doesn't check how much you type. The old gets function reads a name into a fifty character buffer. Type two hundred characters and it writes past the end and corrupts memory. That's a real security hole.

Here's the safe version. fgets takes the buffer and its size, so it stops before the end no matter what. One quirk: it keeps the newline you pressed, so check the last character and swap it for a null terminator.
The whole fix is passing the size of the buffer as the limit. gets never knew the size. fgets can't overflow because you told it where the wall is.
Same program, but now no input can ever escape the buffer. That's the habit to keep.
